summary: This sermon argues that solitude is not merely a therapeutic practice but a training ground for spiritual warfare. Using Jesus' temptation in the wilderness as the model, the pastor teaches that solitude is where Christians can become aware of how the enemy distracts and deceives them away from God's purposes through subtle lies about desires, truth, and abundant life.
key_points: Jesus was led by the Spirit into solitude to confront Satan at the beginning of his ministry
The enemy prefers to distract us subtly rather than confront us directly
Three categories of deception: satisfying desires apart from God, redefining good and evil, and seeking God's gifts without His presence
Solitude reveals the lies we are believing one chain-link at a time before we become enslaved
Following Jesus' example means confronting spiritual enemies through intentional solitude
big_idea: Solitude is a training ground for battle against the distraction and deception of the enemy, where believers can become aware of how Satan seeks to lead them away from God's purposes and toward destruction through subtle lies.
title: SOLITUDE: Encountering the Enemy
